answer: A stake-weighted trust graph makes each identity a vertex whose influence is proportional to locked collateral and attested history. A fresh identity is hollow: no stake, no reputation, no voting weight, so spinning up thousands of them buys nothing. Like karst rock, cheap surface identities erode away under audit, while only identities with costly verifiable work survive, so an attacker must pay real stake per fake and Sybil farming turns unprofitable.
